gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-nandinagari: Approachable is the first word for Noto Sans Nandinagari, but Styro up top is the opposite: retro, crowded, almost touching. Noto Sans Nandinagari keeps its openings generous at every weight, so paragraphs of it read like a window left ajar.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-newa: Styro hits with a retro, commanding punch, its letters jammed together with barely a gap inside. And Noto Sans Newa answers by letting its lowercase e open wide, with tall bowls, which is the real tension here.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-nushu: Noto Sans Nushu reads modern and lofty, its terminals held far from the stroke and its x-height towering. Styro, by contrast, packs its letters tight and closed, so the two feel like a shout and an easy exhale.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-ogham: Noto Sans Ogham reads wide open and tall, almost bold. Styro is the one for retro, crowded display letters with tight shapes, while Noto Sans Ogham gives its wide-gapped e and towering bodies the job of everything quieter.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-ol-chiki: Retro swagger meets open space, with Styro's crowded letters set against curve tails pulled well back. Noto Sans Ol Chiki turns words into solid blocks.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-old-hungarian: Approachable is how Noto Sans Old Hungarian feels, with large open counters in its tall a, e and s that hold up at tiny sizes. And Styro, retro and tightly packed, gives it something commanding to lean against.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-old-italic: Noto Sans Old Italic is contemporary and compact. Styro does retro, commanding display work with tightly closed letters, while Noto Sans Old Italic keeps curve endings well apart and its lowercase nearly as tall as the capitals.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-old-north-arab: Styro's letters are jammed so close they nearly touch. Its retro, commanding display shapes do the shouting, while Noto Sans Old North Arabian settles into a dense, tall lowercase band with terminals flaring outward.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-old-permic: Styro crowds its retro, commanding letters together until the e and c barely have a gap in them. Noto Sans Old Permic stays friendly over a long page, its rounded forms open to the side.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-old-persian: Retro and tightly packed, then wide open. Noto Sans Old Persian lets its counters breathe into the white space, so a long passage feels lofty and light under Styro's crowded heading.
